core_source_freeze.missing_set: missingAll: every missing object of the store, walked from ALL present roots
core_source_freeze.opaque_set: opaqueRelevant: the missing trees and commits that hide names, walked from the PINNED root only

semantics_changed_vs_v3.PM07-full-all-opaque-gate: re-anchored and re-worded: the name-hiding (opaque) walk is rooted at the PINNED root only, so the mutant roots it at every present root. The store-wide missing set already starts from every present root, so that part of the mutant changes nothing. The old prose called the mutant globally redundant; with the v7 core that is no longer true, the primary 47 may still survive, and no kill is presumed. The discriminator is an unselected REF tree hole together with a fabricated citation, which lies OUTSIDE the finite 47 (a wave-3 supplement).
semantics_changed_vs_v3.PM08-no-lazy-fetch-review-only: the scope is now the candidate's repository-reading wrappers: the wrappers carry --no-lazy-fetch, so a missing promisor object is not fetched through the promisor remote on the paths those wrappers read. It is a manual reading, not a proof about every git call. Unchanged: review-only, no alternatives, no source or wiring assertion, 0 executions, killed false, uncredited.

legacy_harness_fix.hazard: with the round-24 scoped retirement of M14/M22/M27/M29 the mutant ids are full names (M01-replace-objects, ...); a selector that names only the numeric part (--only M01) selected nothing, the run still executed the pristine grid and exited 0 with an empty inventory: a silent pass that looks like a calibration success.
legacy_harness_fix.fix: an empty selection is could-not-evaluate (exit 2), decided BEFORE the source is read, before the pristine run and before any grid call; the 27 operators and the retirement history are preserved; no other argument is validated and no expectation changes.
legacy_harness_fix.proof: legacy-empty-selection-proof.txt: before = exit 0 with 1 grid invocation and an empty inventory; after = exit 2 with 0 grid invocations.

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell whose audited repository is promisor-marked: a refusal on the metadata alone turns each of them into exit 2
mutants_v4.semantic: promisor metadata alone (extensions.partialClone, remote.*.promisor, partialclonefilter, paired .promisor+.pack) is not a refusal: a complete promisor-marked repository keeps the verdict of its full-clone twin

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell with an unresolved citation whose ordinary verdict is a failed finding: the errata-corrected absent hash is refused before the ledger is consulted, and the opaque cells misclassify an absence that a missing tree may conceal
mutants_v4.semantic: the unknown rule covers a locally unresolved citation that names unavailable referenced content; it must not cover every absent citation, or the historical errata-marked clone (absent hash corrected by errata) would stop being an ordinary failed finding. The mutant refuses every absent (or unknown) citation, before the errata ledger is consulted.

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell whose required evidence is unavailable and whose verdict must be could-not-evaluate
mutants_v4.semantic: objects the audit actually reads must be available: a missing required commit/tree/blob/report object is could-not-evaluate (exit 2), never a clean or failed verdict. This mutant removes the store's missing-object computation (the completeness element); PM04 removes the decision that uses it. Both attack the same verdict surface, so the grid kills them alike: one of them surviving is not evidence about the other.

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell whose unresolved citation names unavailable referenced content
mutants_v4.semantic: a locally unresolved citation that names unavailable referenced local content is could-not-evaluate rather than proved absent; the mutant accepts it as absent and reports an ordinary failed finding

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell whose citation resolves only in the second audited repository
mutants_v4.semantic: a citation missing in one audited repository but present in the other audited repository is resolvable; the mutant consults the first repository only

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell whose verdict must be could-not-evaluate because a required read failed
mutants_v4.semantic: a failing read of the object the audit needs is could-not-evaluate; the mutant swallows the failure and guesses a value, turning an unavailable object into a verdict

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: the closest in-grid surface: the cells with a hole on an unselected branch. The 47 cells may not distinguish the mutant at all, because the discriminating fixture (an unselected REF tree hole plus a fabricated citation) is a wave-3 supplement outside the finite grid
mutants_v4.semantic: the name-hiding walk (the missing trees and commits that may conceal the dependency names of an unresolved citation) is rooted at the pinned lane/fleet root ONLY; the mutant roots that walk at every present root of the store, so a hole behind an unselected ref becomes relevant to the audit. The store-wide missing set already starts from every present root, so that part of the mutant changes nothing; the discriminator is an unselected REF tree hole together with a fabricated citation, which lies OUTSIDE the primary 47 cells (a wave-3 supplement). On the primary 47 this mutant may therefore survive: no kill is presumed, and the final run decides.

review-only note, uncredited: the candidate's repository-reading wrappers carry --no-lazy-fetch, so a missing promisor object is not fetched through the promisor remote (transport, repository programs, signatures) on the paths those wrappers read. This is a manual reading of the candidate's isolation flags, not a proof about every git call. The element is not part of the executed inventory: no mutant is built, no grid invocation is made for it, and it is never credited with a kill

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell whose locally present blob must stay an ordinary wrong-type finding
mutants_v4.semantic: the bare full-hash lookup stays unpeeled: a citation of a locally present blob resolves as found; peeling it to ^{commit} turns a present blob into a missing object

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell whose verdict depends on the opaque non-leaf rule
mutants_v4.semantic: when a citation is unresolved, a missing tree or commit may conceal the dependency names, so the citation is unevaluable (exit 2); the mutant ignores that hole and reports an ordinary failed finding. A known-present blob that merely fails commit peeling keeps its wrong-type finding either way.

mutants_v4.attribution_basis: every cell whose audited repository holds a hole, whatever verdict the cell expects: the gate is unconditional
mutants_v4.semantic: no missing-object state may be an unconditional audit precondition: an unrelated blob hole next to a fabricated citation keeps the ordinary failed finding, and an unused tree hole next to fully resolved citations keeps the clean verdict; the mutant refuses on any hole
